title: Your first Deployment and Service on Kubernetes

ticket.subject: sensor-api on the cluster, behind a Service
body: The image `ghcr.io/contoso/sensor-api:0.1` is in our registry and the platform team gave us a namespace on
the cluster (we use `default` for now). The previous intern started `k8s/deployment.yaml`; please finish it:
- **Two pods** of sensor-api, so one can be lost without an outage. The app listens on port **8000**:
declare it on the container, named `http`.
- **A Service** `sensor-api` in `k8s/service.yaml`, on port 80, that sends traffic to the pods' `http` port.
- Apply the folder, then look at what the cluster made of it: the pods (`kubectl get pods`), one object in
detail (`kubectl describe`), and the Service's endpoints, which must list both pods.
This is the lab's simulated cluster: nothing is deployed, and your manifests are read, never executed.

acceptance.text: The sensor-api Deployment runs ghcr.io/contoso/sensor-api:0.1 on two ready pods, none of them failing.

checks.fail: kubectl apply, get pods, describe and get endpoints were not all run.

hints: A Deployment keeps `replicas` copies of its pod `template` running; its `selector.matchLabels` must match the template's labels.
Declare the port on the container: `ports: [{name: http, containerPort: 8000}]` (as a YAML list). Naming it lets the Service say `targetPort: http`.

A Service finds its pods by labels: its `selector` must match the pod template's labels exactly (`app.kubernetes.io/name: sensor-api`). `port` is what callers use, `targetPort` is where the app listens.
`kubectl apply -f k8s/` applies every file of the folder; `kubectl rollout status deployment/sensor-api` waits for the pods; `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows them with their IPs.
`kubectl describe deployment sensor-api` or `kubectl describe pod NAME` explains a pod that is not ready (an image that cannot be pulled, for example).
`kubectl get endpoints sensor-api` lists the pod IP:port pairs the Service sends traffic to. Empty means its selector matches no ready pod.
